title_suffix: Indexed project knowledge, scoped agent context, and measurable faster goal execution
summary: OSpec 1.7.0 makes project knowledge durable after archive and makes goal execution materially leaner without removing workflow gates. Finalize/archive now refreshes the project feature index and the AI index records project documents plus archived changes, so future agents can locate implemented behavior without replaying old conversations. Worker and reviewer packets start from scoped evidence, reviews remain independent and combined, documentation obligations can be enforced per task, and execution metrics make context size and duration visible. In the first controlled A/B benchmark, input tokens fell by 28.19% to 48.52% depending on document size (40.03% combined) while all planted defects were still detected. These are initial benchmark results, not a guarantee for every repository.
new: Finalize/archive now regenerates docs/project/feature-index.md. SKILL.index.json includes project documents and archived changes, allowing both humans and AI agents to locate existing behavior from an index instead of scanning every archived change.

Task review and final review automatically produce scoped review packages with the dispatch commit, current HEAD, workspace status, diff stat, target-file diff, untracked target files, out-of-scope changes, and dirty-at-dispatch attribution warnings.
Goal runs write artifacts/agents/execution-metrics.json with dispatch packet, worker report, review packet/package byte counts and task duration evidence.

Task graphs can declare documentation_updates. When enabled, each path must be project-relative, safe, exist, and also appear in the task target_files; undeclared documentation obligations block status, finalize, and archive.
Added a mechanical worker tier for narrow documentation-only tasks while keeping implementation reasoning tiers and specialist reviewers unchanged.

Added authoritative usage ingestion through automatic OSPEC_USAGE_FILE sidecars for command runners and the manual ospec execute complete/review --usage-file fallback. Normalized counters are aggregated without copying raw provider responses.

Added grouped repair waves. ospec execute repair converts the complete NEEDS_CHANGES final-review findings list into one repair task and reuses the normal dispatch, completion, combined task review, and final re-review gates.

Added an opt-in adaptive document-review policy. The backward-compatible default remains always; adaptive uses deterministic inline preflight only when the target document explicitly declares low or no risk and no API, security, migration, data, architecture, external-integration, broad-surface, or explicit high-risk signal is present.

Added configurable logical model profiles for mechanical, standard, strong_reasoning, review, and final_review roles. Harness-specific model names come only from .skillrc workflow configuration; missing mappings explicitly fall back to the harness default.

Reviewers now produce human-readable Markdown plus sibling structured findings JSON with stable IDs, severity, category, file/line evidence, requirement references, and repair scope. Legacy Markdown is converted to a compatibility sidecar before grouped repair.

Command-based worker and review runs receive OSPEC_USAGE_FILE for automatic authoritative usage ingestion. Metrics record source, observed fields, model-profile aggregation, and complete/partial/missing coverage.
improved: Worker packets now carry task context, global constraints, interfaces, target files, and indexed knowledge locations. Workers treat the packet as the task brief and open core change or project documents only for a named gap instead of reloading every document by default.

Task review and whole-change final review each use one combined spec-compliance and code-quality pass. Reviewer prompts remain independent and read-only, require file/line evidence, and can return CANNOT_VERIFY_FROM_TASK_SCOPE rather than guessing from incomplete scope.
Plan preflight checks cross-task contradictions, missing interfaces and constraints, task sizing, and documentation ownership before dispatch.

Dispatch records capture one Git porcelain-v2 snapshot for the full baseline SHA and clean/dirty attribution, with a compatibility fallback for older Git. Same-stage execution metrics are written in one batch instead of rewriting the metrics file per entry.

Review packages reuse one porcelain-v2 snapshot for the current HEAD and complete workspace status, and skip the empty commit-log command when HEAD still equals the dispatch baseline. The deterministic 7-repeat fixture reduced the typical review Git sequence from 6 processes to 4 and its median time from 412.84ms to 278.01ms (32.66%) while retaining baseline validation, diff stat, full diff, untracked files, renames, and out-of-scope evidence.

Controlled context benchmark: combined input tokens decreased from 161,593 to 96,906 (40.03%); input plus output decreased from 162,985 to 97,649 (40.09%); uncached input plus output decreased 37.14%; tool calls decreased 73.33%; model-stage elapsed time decreased 34.52%. Small and medium fixtures measured 28.19% and 48.52% input-token reductions respectively, with one live A/B sample per scenario.

Controller-only performance follow-up reduced measured dispatch fixed overhead by 38.90% across the two deterministic fixtures and reduced the Git phase by 44.21%, without changing packet content or consuming additional model tokens.

Reduced the packaged root SKILL.md from 30,432 bytes and 410 lines to 8,159 bytes and 96 lines (73.19% fewer bytes). The compact router keeps invariant safety rules in root context and routes stage details through the project index, feature index, current packet, for-ai guides, and CLI help; byte reduction is not claimed as an identical token reduction.

Claude hook bootstrap context is no longer repeated on every user prompt. Static Announce-Before-Act and Brainstorm-First context is limited to startup, clear, and compact; UserPromptSubmit emits only dynamic pending-decision context, while PreToolUse(Task) retains the hard dispatch block. In deterministic no-decision 10/20/40-turn simulations, direct injected bytes decreased 90.00%/95.00%/97.50%, with zero model calls; actual billed-token savings still depend on caching and compaction.

Documentation contracts now capture normalized content hashes at dispatch and completion. New runs reject declared documentation files that exist but did not change meaningfully; legacy in-progress goals without baselines remain compatible and are explicitly marked unverified.

Feature indexes now link each archived feature directly to its declared durable project documents. SKILL.index.json document entries can expose feature, module, and alias metadata for more precise human and AI retrieval.

The context benchmark accepts an explicit baseline ref, resolves it to an immutable commit, adds a large-document scenario, and reports means, medians, ranges, standard deviations, paired reduction distributions, and 95% confidence intervals when repeated samples are available.

Every successfully archived classic change and goal now receives one localized docs/project/changes/<archive-path>.md containing its summary, affected areas, implementation files, verification commands, durable project-document links, and archived evidence. Feature and AI indexes link this per-change document directly.
fixed: Updated js-yaml to 4.3.0 and Vitest to 4.1.10, removing the known production and development dependency advisories reported by npm audit at release time.

Archived features no longer disappear from the generated project indexes when an unrelated proposal or project document has damaged frontmatter; index generation degrades safely and preserves valid archive knowledge.
Session re-entry preserves the projectSession snapshot, including knowledge index paths and indexed document/archive counts, across dispatch, launch, review, and handoff artifacts.
Legacy configurations that still list sequential spec_compliance_review and code_quality_review steps normalize to the single final_review gate.
Blocker records now state whether human judgment is required and distinguish missing context from an external blocker.
Index generation and the standalone build-index tool reuse one archive snapshot per write, avoiding inconsistent or repeated archive scans.
Model selection is now visible in worker and reviewer artifacts as a logical profile, configured model, and selection source, preventing silent reliance on an unknown harness default.

Adaptive document review remains conservative: only a target document that explicitly declares risk_level low or none can use inline preflight. Missing or unparseable context and English, Chinese, Japanese, or Arabic risk signals force specialist review instead of silently weakening the gate.
Partial provider usage no longer makes unreported token, tool-call, turn, or elapsed counters appear to be authoritative measured zeros.

Archive now preflights index and documentation writes before moving an active change, then verifies after rebuild that archived_changes, SKILL.index.json.documents, the generated change document, and feature-index.md all reference the completed change.

Read-only index snapshots now recover existing generated change-document paths from archive layout, preventing index check from repeatedly reporting a freshly written index as stale. OSpec cleans only stale files marked as its own archive-knowledge output and preserves human-owned documents.

Archive preflight now probes every managed output directory before moving the active change and refuses to overwrite a human-owned file at the generated per-change knowledge path. Index rebuilds enforce the same ownership check as a second line of defense.
Release repository export now includes scripts/benchmark-context-efficiency.js, with inventory and real-sync assertions preventing future release syncs from deleting the benchmark runner.

Added a network-free upgrade regression matrix for 1.5.0, 1.5.1, 1.6.0, and 1.6.1 projects, covering nested layout, custom configuration and disabled hooks, active goal/change state, archived content, index generation, per-change knowledge documents, and a second idempotent ospec update.
docs: Updated the root skill, goal skill, AI guides, execution protocols, workflow conventions, README, source, dist, tests, and all four managed languages for the scoped-context and single-review workflow.

Added docs/benchmarks/context-efficiency-2026-07-11.zh-CN.md with the benchmark method, raw aggregate measurements, token budget accounting, quality gates, limitations, deterministic dispatch profiling, reproduction commands, and full verification record.

Added reusable scripts/benchmark-context-efficiency.js. Live runs require an explicit model, isolate child sessions, capture authoritative usage, and counterbalance baseline/current ordering across scenarios and repetitions; every dry-run also records the 7-repeat review Git strategy comparison.

Documented hook context deduplication, the lean root router, usage ingestion, grouped repair, adaptive review policy, and configurable logical model routing across the root/goal skills, managed AI guides and execution protocols, CLI help, README files, and all four managed languages.

Rewrote the main README goal section in user-facing language around when to use a goal, how to start, what the user must do, what the AI handles, safety levels, progress, pause, and resume without requiring controller terminology.

Documented the one-change-one-document archive rule and the distinction between generated change summaries and required human-maintained architecture, API, module, and operational docs in English, Chinese, Japanese, and Arabic guides, protocols, conventions, skills, and READMEs.
Bumped the package, CLI, lockfile, and English, Chinese, Japanese, and Arabic installation examples to 1.7.0.
